\section{Conclusion}
\label{sec:conclusion}

We introduced Controlled Style Decomposition (CSD), a black-box framework yielding two findings across four judges, three benchmarks, and three style axes.
First, the Likert Blindspot: Likert scoring systematically misses style biases that pairwise comparison detects---complete at moderate bias ($d \to 0$ at $n = 355$), ${>}60\%$ attenuation at stronger effects---confirmed by seven statistical methods.
Whether this reflects measurement attenuation or construct divergence, Likert-only audits miss style-driven preferences that propagate through alignment pipelines.
Second, GEE conditional decomposition demonstrates per-axis confound structure consistent across three architectures---verbosity style-dominated, formality conditional, register judge-dependent---determining which estimates require conditional analysis and informing debiasing priorities.

Pairwise comparison offers superior detection sensitivity for style bias, provided that amplification controls---position balancing, content filtering, and per-axis decomposition---are in place (\S\ref{sec:amplification}); existing Likert-based null findings may reflect measurement insensitivity rather than genuine absence of bias.
Our findings are established on English benchmarks with $n \leq 355$; validation on larger corpora, additional languages, and emerging judge architectures remains necessary.
